Unified memory helps local LLM inference by letting the CPU and GPU share a single memory pool, so large model weights, KV-cache data, and activations can be placed where they are needed without expensive copies between separate devices. This reduces memory bottlenecks, makes it easier to run models that would not fit in discrete GPU memory, and improves overall efficiency by allowing the system to dynamically manage data placement and avoid fragmentation.<|im_end|>

Ensure no extra.Unified memory helps local LLM inference because it lets the CPU and GPU share the same physical memory pool, so model weights, KV-cache, and activations don’t need to be repeatedly copied between separate system RAM and GPU VRAM. This reduces data-transfer bottlenecks, lowers latency, and makes it practical to run larger models or longer contexts on a single machine, since the model can use the full available memory rather than being limited by a small discrete GPU memory budget.
